title: Signal Message Writing
source: Defence Forces Service Writing Manual 2024 (JP-04), Chapter 4
notes: Signal messages use Form J/Sigs/84 (Annex A to Chapter 4).

rules.title: Signal message text is in capital letters throughout
rules.description: Capital letters are used for every letter in and outside the text, equally for handwritten and typewritten messages.

rules.title: Precedence must be FLASH, IMMEDIATE, PRIORITY or ROUTINE
rules.description: The four degrees of precedence given to messages are FLASH, IMMEDIATE, PRIORITY and ROUTINE.

check.where: Precedence line of the message form.

rules.title: DTG must use the format DDHHMM zone month year
rules.description: A DTG consists of 3 pairs of digits (date, hour, minutes) followed by a time zone suffix letter, the first 3 letters of the month and the last 2 figures of the year, e.g. 051230C Mar 23.

check.where: Date Time Group on the message.

rules.notes: The manual instructs that the first 3 letters of the month be in capitals but its own examples use title case (e.g. 051230C Mar 23); the pattern accepts both.

rules.title: DTG is inserted by the releasing officer after signature
rules.description: It is the responsibility of the releasing officer to insert the DTG after he/she signs the message.

rules.title: GMT is used for messages crossing time zones or including addressees outside Kenya
rules.description: GMT (suffix) is used for messages that pass from one time zone to another, whose text relates to another time zone, or that include any addressee outside Kenya.

rules.title: Addresses in signal messages are in capitals with spaces between words
rules.description: Capital letters are used throughout; spaces are left between words and between letters and figures, but no spaces between letters of an abbreviation.

rules.title: Addresses must use authorized abbreviated titles
rules.description: The authorized abbreviated titles for commands, formations, bases, units and establishments shown at Annex B to Chapter 16 are to be used in the address.

rules.title: Multiple address messages indicate ACTION and INFORMATION addressees
rules.description: In a multiple address message each addressee must be indicated as 'ACTION' or 'INFORMATION'.

rules.title: Book messages carry the word BOOK in message instructions
rules.description: For a book message, 'BOOK' is to be inserted in the 'MESSAGE INSTRUCTIONS' box on the message form.

rules.title: Exercise messages are identified by the word EXERCISE
rules.description: Exercise messages are identified by the word 'EXERCISE' followed by the exercise identification, inserted as the first words of the text following the INFO line or privacy marking.

rules.title: Drill messages begin and end with the word DRILL
rules.description: The text of a message intended only for the training of communication personnel is to begin and end with the word 'DRILL'.

check.where: Start and end of message text.

rules.title: Casualty exercise messages must not use real personnel names
rules.description: In casualty messages used for exercise purposes the names and particulars of serving personnel must NOT be used.
rules.notes: Human review: names and particulars of serving personnel must NOT be used in exercise casualty messages.
